executiveSummary: GM0755 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, eight neighbourhoods, two BAG places, 16 BRT settlements, three NWB links, null semantics, local reconciliation, exact zero-intensity behavior, causal ledgers and sustained-water repair guard are coherent. Release remains correction-required for three spatial-evidence defects. First, the named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset assigns Boekel persistent municipality-wide inundation stress without selecting the municipality's actual east-to-west Leijgraaf/De Aa, Peelrand-fault, regional-water or sewer pathway: the internal normalized amplitude is 0.902961 at both T+24 and T+72, with 6,931 then 7,010 modeled people under pressure and 67,459 then 272,616 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours. Second, river, pluvial and heat neighbourhood maps use the identical seeded order despite the municipality's own map distinguishing the Boekel bowl/fault zone, stony core, Boschberg nuisance area, Venhorst heat/drought/cloudburst exposure, wet wijst zones and highly permeable dry sandy areas. Third, a focused synthetic T+24 ignition inside an official TOP10NL mixed-forest polygon and BU07550009 makes the source neighbourhood rank second while Venhorst, 3.409 km from the source, ranks first; no source or fuel geometry controls the local allocation. Official public context is valuable but non-causal: the current snapshot intersects 92 weirs, one sewer pump, 24 antenna installations, two government-service records, four DUO education locations and no RIVM acute-hospital record. Zero acute-hospital records and empty drainage-provider lookup are not zero health care or zero drainage. Physical Enexis, Brabant Water, municipal sewer, telecom, care and emergency-supply topology, current state, backups, stocks, crews and restoration commitments remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented; all eight utility views correctly call their shared N605/N277 road flows logical transfer proxies.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Brabant-Noord 2024–2027
supports: The regional worst-case flood is high Maas/EDO 36, while Aa, Dommel and Dieze regional barriers are separate and local likelihood and impact can differ from the regional worst case.
The nature-fire reference is a 200-hectare forest/heath fire during extreme drought, very strong wind and difficult access; vegetation, accessibility, escape routes and response capacity matter.

The profile covers extreme rain, storm, heat, drought, winter conditions, energy/gas, drinking water, wastewater, telecom/ICT and cyber disruption and cascading dependencies; its reference service durations make a 72-hour exercise relevant but do not calibrate any exact GM0755 curve.

This is four-year strategic scenario/expert context, not a live warning, local footprint, probability surface, asset inventory or restoration commitment. No explicit machine API or redistribution licence accompanies the PDF.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatonderlegger voor de gemeente Boekel
supports: The municipal map distinguishes a bowl-shaped water-stagnation/nuisance zone east of the N277 and in core Boekel between the Peelrand fault and built core, plus increasingly heat- and water-sensitive stony centre/eastern neighbourhoods.

It identifies Venhorst as structurally more drought/heat stressed and increasingly exposed to nuisance from extreme showers, highly permeable horst sands as extremely drought-sensitive, and fault-adjacent seepage/wijst areas as locally wetter.

At De Burgt it distinguishes a western infiltrating bowl and short-duration nuisance from a high-wet eastern side, demonstrating that local groundwater and runoff do not follow one municipality or neighbourhood seed.

The PDF is authoritative commissioned spatial/planning context, but no native machine GIS, explicit reuse licence, fixed update cadence, event definition, grid resolution, depth unit, no-data convention or current hydraulic state is published with it.

evidenceSources.title: Toekomstvisie — De kracht van Boekel
supports: Boekel is a rural municipality with agrarian land, small forests and the Peelrand fault; characteristic watercourses flow east to west into the Leijgraaf and De Aa, while forest landscapes lie in the north and south.
The municipality identifies heat, drought, extreme rain and water nuisance and aims for a partly climate-adaptive sewer and water-and-soil-led development.
Solar generation materially loads and overloads the local electricity network and reinforcement is necessary; this is planning context rather than outage state, spare capacity or disaster fragility.

The vision also identifies ageing, reduced mobility, access to care and rural accessibility as local policy concerns. It is a dated policy PDF with no machine API, operational cadence or explicit reuse licence.

evidenceSources.title: De Boschberg — climate-resilient sewer and public-space reconstruction
evidenceSources.edition: live project page inspected 2 September 2026; drawings dated through March 2026
supports: Municipal sewer investigations identify Boschberg in core Boekel as a particular bottleneck, with water on streets more often than elsewhere and private-property nuisance in worse cases.

The current project replaces sewer/public-space elements and publishes dated design sheets; Waterschap Aa en Maas separately documents infiltration sewer and swales and the rainwater/wastewater overflow mechanism.

This is authoritative local engineering/problem context, not a live incident, municipality-wide rain/depth raster, sewer graph, pump state, capacity model or restoration forecast. The page has event-driven updates and no explicit dataset licence.

evidenceSources.title: Waterbericht juni: de droogte slaat toe, waterschap in actie
supports: During the observed June 2025 episode, groundwater fell rapidly, increasingly large watercourses dried, crop demand rose and Maas inflow was maximized.

The water board explicitly states that maximum Maas supply could not reach every area, especially Boekel/Venhorst, Gemert, Landhorst and Veghel; measures included abstraction restrictions and raising weirs.

This is dated observed/operational drought context, not a recurring GM0755 service outage, future forecast, machine feed, drinking-water pressure result or calibration of the canonical heatwave. No fixed update cadence or explicit data licence is stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs

notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.746430, pluvial 0.565939, river 0.285448, coastal 0.011929, heat 0.493328, winter 0.511213, cyber 0.486724, earthquake 0.010749, wildfire 0.117098 and compound 0.960535.

Canonical wildfire is remote smoke/drought context at Boekel: T+24 direct flame is zero, smoke 0.275044 and drought 0.517410. The focused local ignition is a separate reproducibility diagnostic, not an observed incident.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, cumulative burden, route bounds, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0755 pnpm audit:model passed both focused coverage tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 32.74 seconds on the final post-integration rerun.
Every preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every required checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; values are finite and bounded; cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic; and route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles population 11,465, affected population 7,859 and all eight service demand/delivery balances, with maximum observed floating-point discrepancy 8.88e-16.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The named-river screen, identical multi-hazard neighbourhood order and source-insensitive local wildfire allocation contradict Boekel's available spatial mechanisms.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-466 reduces Rhine/Meuse/IJssel exposure to municipality-centre distance from three approximate line segments; no selected EDO 36 defence, Leijgraaf/De Aa connection, fault-zone, depth/arrival/duration/recession surface or regional-water control supports GM0755's persistent result.

At T+24 and T+72 the river preset retains normalized inundation stress 0.902961 and severity 0.285448. Modeled people under pressure rise from 6,931 to 7,010 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours from 67,459 to 272,616.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3447-3461 applies municipality severity through a shared region hash. River, pluvial and heat therefore have the identical exact order: Venhorst; Bovenstehuis/Peelsehuis; rural Venhorst; Arendnest-Zijp; Zandhoek/Peelstraat; Boekel; Logt/Berkhoek; Molenwijk/Elzen/Neerbroek.

At pluvial T+24 Venhorst is 0.447442 while BU07550000 Boekel is sixth at 0.341316, even though E04/E06 distinguish the core/fault-zone and Boschberg mechanisms. The issue is not that Venhorst is safe—E04 also calls it rain-sensitive—but that no hazard-specific surface or catchment controls either value.

A focused synthetic T+24 source [5.6955, 51.624] intersects TOP10NL mixed forest and BU07550009. Direct fire is 0.535503 and municipality severity 0.516517, but the source neighbourhood ranks second at 0.547680 while Venhorst ranks first at 0.603749 from 3.409 km away.
GM0755 emits derived-screening or synthetic rather than unsupported spatial evidence, so the UI safety treatment for unsupported local hazard distribution is not activated.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight balances and dependency stages are inspectable, but their magnitudes are not calibrated to Boekel's providers, water system, facilities, rural access or supply chain.
notes: Compound T+24 availability was power 0.578531, water 0.269890, drainage 0.229789, gas 0.524886, telecom 0.143469, mobility 0.728664, facilities 0.167397 and supply 0.293012.

E03 supports the direction of power/telecom/water/wastewater/mobility cascades; E05–E08 establish network stress, Boschberg sewer coupling, drought supply limits and registered water assets. None calibrates the exact availability, demand, delivery, reserve or repair values.

The causal graph has no named Rioolgemaal Venhorst, weir/catchment chain, Boschberg infiltration sewer/swales, Leijgraaf/De Aa outlet, Enexis Uden supply path, Brabant Water source/pressure zone, antenna power/backhaul, health-care continuity site or food/fuel depot.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve confidence, operations assumptions, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, local context factors, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness affects modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and delayed interventions are labeled bounded scenario assumptions; road-derived utility transfers remain explicit logical proxies.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline and are not observed outage-hours, casualties, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water repair gating behaves consistently, but no local event, asset, access, backup or crew evidence calibrates restoration through T+72.
notes: For river flooding, normalized inundation stress remains 0.902961 through T+72 and recoveryProgress remains exactly zero for all eight services; drainage availability stays 0.268017, while facilities changes from 0.426795 to 0.391868 through dependency dynamics.

For compound, inundation stress remains 0.546417 and recoveryProgress is zero for every service at T+72; telecom remains limiting at 0.141773 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours reach 469,653.
This verifies the sustained-active-water recovery guard. It does not validate the unselected water forcing or imply that all local systems would remain static for 72 hours.

Transient storm, pluvial, winter, wildfire and earthquake exercises recover numerically after their envelopes; heat retains drought stress within its canonical 336-hour event and cyber retains 0.048672 severity at T+72.
No source supplies event-specific damage, live control state, generator/fuel endurance, priority customers, staff, stock, repair access, crews, mutual aid or restoration commitment.

findings.summary: A coarse named-major-river proximity field presents unsupported persistent Boekel inundation without a selected local hydraulic pathway.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-466 uses only municipality-centre distance to three approximate Rhine/Meuse/IJssel line segments. At T+24 and T+72 the canonical river preset reports internal normalized inundation-stress amplitude 0.902961, severity 0.285448 and zero recovery across all services; modeled people under pressure are 6,931 then 7,010 and cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours are 67,459 then 272,616. E03 says the regional worst case is high Maas/EDO 36 and that local impacts differ; E04/E05 instead identify Boekel's fault, bowl, east-to-west Leijgraaf/De Aa and regional-water mechanisms. No selected defence, water level, connected footprint, probability, arrival, duration or recession supports the displayed direct GM0755 amplitude. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared proximity-screen defect, not a claim that Boekel is flood-safe.
findings.action: Mark GM0755 direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel impact unsupported/Unknown and make unsupported direct forcing numerically neutral for operational consequence until an expert selects a named/versioned connected hydraulic scenario. Preserve separately labeled Leijgraaf/De Aa, pluvial, groundwater, sewer and indirect-network context.

findings.summary: One shared neighbourhood hash replaces Boekel's distinct cloudburst, groundwater, drought and heat geographies.
findings.evidence: E04 distinguishes core Boekel's bowl and stony heat/water-sensitive areas, Venhorst's drought/heat/cloudburst stress, permeable dry horst sands, fault-adjacent wet wijst and De Burgt's west/east contrast; E06 identifies Boschberg as a sewer bottleneck with nuisance more often than elsewhere. Nevertheless packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3447-3461 gives river, pluvial and heat the identical exact eight-area T+24 order: Venhorst; Bovenstehuis/Peelsehuis; rural Venhorst; Arendnest-Zijp; Zandhoek/Peelstraat; Boekel; Logt/Berkhoek; Molenwijk/Elzen/Neerbroek. Pluvial severity is 0.447442 in Venhorst and 0.341316 in BU07550000 Boekel. No rain/depth/temperature raster, terrain depression, surface cover, fault, groundwater, sewer catchment, outlet, asset connectivity or control state determines the rank.
findings.action: Label neighbourhood water/heat ranks synthetic and unsupported for dispatch or evacuation. Request the native machine surface behind E04/E06; if unavailable use version-pinned national screening inputs with explicit caveats. Preserve event, metric, grid size, units, edition, no-data, licence and uncertainty, and require tests in which hazard-specific inputs can produce different orders.

findings.summary: An explicit source in a Boekel mixed-forest polygon does not control the neighbourhood map presented as local wildfire impact.
findings.evidence: E02/E05 establish north/south Boekel forest context. A focused synthetic T+24 run put source [5.6955, 51.624] in current TOP10NL mixed-forest object 107870447 and official BU07550009 Verspreide huizen Bovenstehuis en Peelsehuis. The municipality reports direct fire 0.535503, smoke 0.451429, drought 0.517410 and severity 0.516517, but the source neighbourhood ranks second at 0.547680. Venhorst ranks first at 0.603749 although its centre is 3.409 km from the source. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3447-3461 never intersects local source, perimeter or eligible fuel. This is a reproducibility diagnostic, not an observed fire or current forecast.
findings.action: Keep direct-fire neighbourhood ranks visibly synthetic/unsupported and prohibit rank-based operational use. Make local allocation source/perimeter and eligible-fuel aware, while modeling transported smoke, drought, access, extinguishing water and suppression separately.

findings.summary: Ninety-three official water objects improve context but do not establish Boekel drainage performance or the Boschberg failure chain.
findings.evidence: E08 contributes 92 weirs and Rioolgemaal Venhorst inside the generalized boundary; E06 identifies Boschberg sewer overload and private-property nuisance, while E04/E05 distinguish fault, groundwater, streams and climate-adaptive sewer needs. The application correctly marks all public objects affectsSimulation=false. Compound T+24/T+72 drainage availability 0.229789/0.229116 arises from generic equations, not catchment/connectivity, pipe capacity, inlet blockage, infiltration, swales, weir/pump controls, receiving-water level, overflow, emergency power or telemetry. A returned point and displayed status cannot be treated as a complete network or an operating asset.
findings.action: Retain IMWA/DAMO/GWSW objects as partial non-causal context. Obtain a licensed, security-reviewed municipal sewer/stress-test graph and exercise state before causal use; otherwise expose named bounded subsystem assumptions with Unknown connectivity, capacity, backup and state.

findings.summary: Known local electricity-network loading is context, not calibrated baseline capacity, fragility or restoration in the simulation.
findings.evidence: E05 states that solar generation heavily loads/overloads the Boekel electricity network and reinforcement is necessary. A current provider lookup identifies Enexis at one municipal reference point, yet the model has no substation, feeder, transformer, constrained connection, switching, live capacity or priority-customer state. Compound T+24 power availability 0.578531 and T+72 0.571124 are therefore synthetic scenario balances, not an Enexis outage forecast. Planning congestion does not itself prove emergency fragility or current outage.
findings.action: Add dated grid-capacity and static asset data only as non-causal planning context. Use physical or operational effects solely from licensed operator-approved exercise topology/state; otherwise retain service-specific bounded synthetic priors and sensitivity controls with current capacity and restoration explicit Unknown.

findings.summary: The same N605/N277 corridors are cloned across all eight services and cannot represent Boekel's physical utility or response topology.
findings.evidence: Three NWB-derived links totaling nominal 450 connect GM0755 to Maashorst, Gemert-Bakel and Land van Cuijk. The model applies all three to power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply. E03/E05/E08 establish service-specific water, electricity, care/access and cascade concerns, not shared road topology. The engine/UI correctly emit transferSemantics logical-proxy, but road direction, nominal capacity and flow are not feeders, pipes, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food/fuel routes.
findings.action: Keep logical-proxy language and prevent these flows from supporting physical claims. Restrict NWB/NDW to mobility and repair/supply access; add utility/facility edges only from authorized topology or clearly named editable exercise gateways with Unknown capacity/state.

findings.summary: Aggregate vulnerability and public facility/antenna points do not resolve first-72-hour care, communications or household continuity.
findings.evidence: E01/E05 support ageing, one-person households, mobility and care-access context. The deployed public snapshot intersects 24 RDI antenna installations, two government-service records, four DUO education locations and no RIVM acute-hospital location. These records remain non-causal and do not establish coverage, backhaul, operator, load, backup runtime, patient role, shelter designation, staffing, occupancy or supplies. No evidence establishes household medical-electricity need, pharmacy/supermarket/fuel stock, depots, vehicles, facility acceptance or restoration agreements. Facilities 0.167397 and telecom 0.143469 at compound T+24 are synthetic balances, not observed continuity.
findings.action: Keep aggregate context non-individual and public registries display-only. Build a typed dated registry with explicit role/coverage/licence; require authorized GHOR/provider continuity inputs for capacity, occupancy, backup, stock and status, preserving Unknown whenever absent.

findings.summary: Weather, cyber, earthquake and canonical remote-wildfire outputs are exercises rather than Boekel observations or local probabilities.
findings.evidence: E03 supports the relevance of storm, extreme rain, heat, drought, winter, nature fire, energy/water/telecom failure and cyber disruption, but not exact local curves. Canonical weather uses generated envelopes; cyber has no named affected Boekel organization/system; canonical wildfire has zero local flame but T+24 smoke 0.275044/drought 0.517410; canonical Groningen earthquake peaks at 0.010749. E04/E05 describe the Peelrand fault as a geological and hydrological boundary, not evidence that the remote Groningen earthquake preset estimates Boekel earthquake probability or damage. No KNMI valid-time warning, earthquake catalogue event, cyber incident, fire perimeter or operator outage drives these frames.
findings.action: Keep presets visibly synthetic. In a separate live/context mode ingest timestamped KNMI weather/radar and earthquake data with product validity and licence; require a named cyber target/system boundary and a selected fire source/perimeter. Never reinterpret the Peelrand fault's water behavior as an earthquake forecast.

findings.summary: Identity, demography, geography, settlement, public-context provenance and null semantics are inspectable.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 match GM0755/Boekel, 11,465 residents, density 332, 20.7% age 65+, 1,288 one-person households, eight neighbourhoods, two BAG places and 16 BRT settlements. The five-person neighbourhood reconciliation difference is disclosed; two all-missing fields remain null. E08 water objects and other deployed public points retain source/classification/retrieval and affectsSimulation=false. Empty provider/RIVM results are not generalized to absent service.
findings.action: Retain edition, retrieval, licence, coverage, evidence class and null/no-data semantics; refresh at source cadence and rerun focused plus national gates after each snapshot.

findings.summary: The full deterministic, causal and layer-invariance contract passes for Boekel.
findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; zero-intensity output is exact zero; compound T+24 local population/affected/service balances reconcile; explanation ledgers close; event-attributable person-hours are matched no-event essential-service pressure; all eleven layer selections preserve state; and every route says logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic, no-data or exact-zero behavior to hide calibration gaps.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.

No approved GM0755 LIWO/Aa en Maas depth, arrival, duration, defence, Leijgraaf/De Aa backwater, runoff, groundwater or catchment grid is ingested; internal inundation stress is not measured local metres.
Suppressing unsupported Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing must not erase real fault-zone, wijst, high-sand drought, regional-water, Boschberg sewer, pluvial or indirect network mechanisms.
The 2020 municipal climate underlay is authoritative context but its native GIS, exact event/metric, grid resolution, licence, no-data and current validity are unavailable.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, faults, streams, culverts, sewers, forests, fuels, households, workers, visitors or individuals.
The public Waterschapshuis layer is partial; 92 weirs and one sewer pump cannot be interpreted as the complete drainage network or as live operation, connectivity, capacity or emergency power.
Provider polygons identify responsibility at one point, not complete coverage, topology or state; an empty drainage-provider response is Unknown and fixed-media territory is not mobile coverage.
RDI antenna points identify registered installations, not operator ownership, radio coverage, backhaul, power/backup, load, availability or restoration.

No physical Enexis, Brabant Water, municipal wastewater, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, current state, backup, priority-customer list, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse three NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food/fuel routes.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish current closure, timetable/vehicle operation, congestion, evacuation throughput or repair access; no railway station lies inside GM0755.
Facilities and supply lack verified care/shelter roles, beds, staff, acceptance, occupancy, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, current fuel/moisture condition, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the BU07550009 case is explicitly synthetic.
The Peelrand fault evidence concerns geology and groundwater; earthquake lacks a selected local event, ground-motion surface, site response and asset fragility.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Boekel resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, flash runoff, dispatch and restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged drought, displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit hazardous-material, aviation, animal-disease/public-health and other risks present in the wider regional risk profile.
